title: AMLO dismisses Reforma's 60% crime-story as “una volada”
summary: Reacting to a Reforma story on a 60-percent rise in crime incidence, AMLO called the information “una volada” (a fabrication), said “what they hold is not true”, and that the public-security secretary would brief the press the next day with the government's figures.

title: AMLO invokes Lerdo's maxim: “the press regulates itself”
summary: In the first weeks of his term, responding to a news item he called untrue, AMLO said his government would not censor anyone ("no hay censura, cero censura, libertad absoluta"), invoking the maxim attributed to president Sebastián Lerdo de Tejada that "la prensa se regula con la prensa", and added there would be criticism but the government would not promote attacks on the media.

title: AMLO: “there is no longer a sold or rented press”
summary: AMLO asserted that the press in Mexico has entered a new stage: "ya no hay periodismo vendido, no hay prensa vendida ni alquilada", claiming that the relationship between press and power has changed for the better.

title: AMLO says a “fifí press” exists
summary: At the morning press conference, López Obrador stated that a "fifí press" exists and that he did not invent the term, using it to describe outlets and commentators he associated with his political opposition. "Fifí" (originally slang for a pretentious, wealthy person) became a recurring label he applied to critical media over the following years.

title: Pedro Ferriz challenges the “fifís vs. non-fifís” framing
summary: The day after AMLO's "prensa fifí" remark, journalist Pedro Ferriz (Estrella TV) directly asked the president, in the same press conference as the Maldonado exchange above, to stop dividing the press into "fifís" and "non-fifís," noting that six journalists had been killed during the term to that point and that he personally had never taken payment from anyone.

title: Lourdes Maldonado asks AMLO for help in a labor dispute
summary: Journalist Lourdes Maldonado López, identifying herself as a reporter for the Tijuana outlet Séptimo Día, asked President López Obrador for help with a years-long labor dispute against Jaime Bonilla (then a Morena senator and later Baja California governor), saying she even feared for her life. AMLO asked his communications coordinator to follow up. Maldonado was murdered outside her home in Tijuana on 2022-01-23; this 2019 exchange was widely re-cited afterward as a press-freedom case.

title: Jorge Ramos disputes homicide figures on his first mañanera visit
summary: In his first mañanera appearance, Univision anchor Jorge Ramos disputed AMLO's claims of progress on violence, citing the government's own security-cabinet homicide figures (8,524 killings in the term's first three months). A rapid back-and-forth over the exact statistics followed, with AMLO replying that, on his government's own figures, the situation had been controlled — "No estoy diciendo, que quede claro, que está resuelto el problema, lo que estoy diciendo es que hemos mantenido los niveles que existían" and "yo tengo otra información." Coverage of the visit also noted a separate exchange, later the same week, about press criticism of AMLO more broadly.

title: AMLO defends the mañanera press against a columnist's claim
summary: Days after Jorge Ramos's first mañanera appearance (2019-04-12, see incidents_groundtruth.yaml 2019-04-12_jorge-ramos-homicide-data), AMLO said he had seen a columnist claiming that the journalists who come to the morning conference were not good journalists and that only Jorge Ramos was; AMLO said he respectfully disagreed and considered the assembled press good and prudent journalists. The expected phrase is the columnist's, quoted and contradicted by AMLO — included as a documented defense/negation edge case, not as a hostility hit.

title: AMLO refers to a “racket of journalism”
summary: Responding to a question about alleged health-sector layoffs, AMLO said the coverage was "propaganda" aimed at hurting his government, and referred to a "hampa del periodismo" (a "racket"/"underworld" of journalism), adding that "la calumnia cuando no mancha, tizna" (slander stains even without proof). The phrase drew criticism from journalists and commentators over the following days, including a direct challenge at the following Monday's conference (see the 2019-05-27 entry below).

title: AMLO attributes “hampa del periodismo” to Enrique Krauze
summary: Asked by a reporter about the backlash to the previous week's "hampa del periodismo" remark — including criticism from former president Vicente Fox — AMLO said the phrase was strong but attributed its coinage to historian Enrique Krauze. Krauze publicly stated on social media that he had not coined it.

title: AMLO recalls his idea of taxing columnists and media
summary: AMLO recalled having said that the government should charge a tax to columnists and media, because many outlets obtained their income from criticizing him ("nos convertimos en una de las industrias más importantes para muchos medios de información"), mentioning columnists earning 200, 300 or 500 thousand pesos a month; he said that continues but no longer has any effect and newspapers fare badly.

title: AMLO calls a Riva Palacio column “cretinismo”
summary: Responding to a column by Raymundo Riva Palacio ("El negocio de las Mañaneras") alleging that businesses paid to have planted questions asked at the morning conferences, AMLO called the claim "cretinismo" (a step beyond mere cynicism, in his framing) and said it showed "la falta de respeto" and "desfachatez." In December 2024, a Mexican court ruled in Riva Palacio's favor in a rights-violation complaint over presidential statements about him.

title: Denise Dresser raises the Aguayo-Moreira defamation case
summary: Columnist and academic Denise Dresser, self-identifying "proudly" with Reforma and Proceso, raised the defamation case brought by former Coahuila governor Humberto Moreira against academic Sergio Aguayo over corruption reporting; a second reporter followed up citing Dresser by name. AMLO gave a lengthy account of the case's political history without directly criticizing Dresser.
named: Denise Dresser; Sergio Aguayo; Reforma; Proceso

title: AMLO challenges Reforma to report on the presidential-plane sale
summary: Commenting on the sale of the presidential plane, AMLO said Reforma had stayed silent — even applauded — when the plane was bought, yet now headlines the sale as “Sablazo, extorsión, influyentismo” (a gouge, extortion, crony influence); he said he would invite Reforma to write a report on whether buying the plane had been right.

title: AMLO links media discontent to the official-advertising cut
summary: AMLO said the media's discontent was because the official advertising budget had been cut ("se bajó el presupuesto de publicidad") and asked rhetorically whether the government would give instructions to make the advertising agreement "más jugoso" in exchange for better treatment; he answered that they did not come to transform things that way and that he exercises his right of reply.

title: AMLO: “we censor no one” — and criticizes media bias
summary: Discussing press treatment of his government, AMLO cited that Carmen Aristegui "también la censuraron" (by previous actors, in his account) and claimed "nosotros no censuramos a nadie, a nadie", adding that there is a campaign against him and that media coverage has "un sesgo, no hay objetividad". A claim of non-censorship combined with criticism of media bias; frame D (press-freedom concept).

title: AMLO: Ciro Gómez Leyva and others “became conservatives”
summary: AMLO said radio, television and press did not understand the new reality and many opted for lies; he singled out Ciro Gómez Leyva as coming from professional, independent journalism and said "se fueron volviendo conservadores, se cansaron de ser como eran", contrasting with the press of the Reforma era and the restored Republic.

title: AMLO: the world's most famous newspapers “lie, slander”
summary: In a COVID-era passage on a worldwide ethical crisis in information handling, AMLO said the world's most famous newspapers "mienten, calumnian", naming The New York Times, The Washington Post, the Financial Times and El País, and called for an "autocrítica" from them for the return to the "nueva normalidad". (Corroborated in the prior session by ~6 Spanish-language news outlets; URLs pending the re-run in step 3.)
named: The New York Times; The Washington Post; Financial Times; El País

title: The “Bloque Opositor Amplio” document is presented
summary: Presidential spokesman Jesús Ramírez Cuevas read out, at AMLO's request, a confidential document titled "Rescatemos a México" proposing a "Bloque Opositor Amplio" (BOA) to remove Morena from its legislative majority in 2021 and recall AMLO's mandate in 2022; the document listed "medios de comunicación, comunicadores afines" (aligned media/commentators) among the actors it proposed organizing. Named institutions, politicians and businesspeople publicly denied involvement afterward. Because the media component is one piece of a broader alleged political alliance rather than a standalone press-hostility statement, this entry's target is more diffuse than the others in this file.

title: AMLO calls Reforma “the bulletin of conservatism in Mexico”
summary: Commenting on media attention to his everyday actions (lowering the car window, greetings), AMLO said the "voceros del conservadurismo" are very attentive to everything he does, that this surely appeared in Reforma — "que es el boletín del conservadurismo en México" — and that foreign papers are similar because the potentados no longer rule.

title: AMLO calls Reforma an “immundo pasquín” over the Macuspana story
summary: Responding to a Reforma front-page story alleging a 223-million-peso embezzlement in Macuspana, Tabasco (AMLO's hometown, where his sister-in-law held municipal office), AMLO called the claim unproven and described Reforma as a "boletín del conservadurismo y del salinismo" and "un pasquín inmundo, sin ética, sin profesionalismo." This is the first of three "pasquín inmundo" episodes in this file (see also 2020-11-09 re El Universal, 2022-03-01 re Reforma again, and 2024-08-06 re Proceso).

title: AMLO accuses the Financial Times of acting “without ethics” over the neoliberal model
summary: Answering on economic policy, AMLO said the Financial Times always pushed the failed neoliberal model and should apologize to the people of Mexico; he held that “the Financial Times, like other famous newspapers, without ethics, have not done their self-criticism”, also naming the New York Times, the Washington Post, the Wall Street Journal and Reforma.
named: Financial Times; The New York Times; The Washington Post; The Wall Street Journal; Reforma

title: AMLO calls El Universal the “other immundo pasquín”
summary: Questioned about an El Universal report that presidential personal secretary Alejandro Esquer had hired shell companies as Morena's treasurer during the 2018 campaign, AMLO called the paper "el otro pasquín inmundo, El Universal" (echoing the term he had used against Reforma two months earlier) and framed both papers' owners as leaders of the opposition to his government.

title: AMLO calls a Bloomberg report an “excess” meant “to hurt Mexico”
summary: On a Bloomberg agency report, AMLO said most people never even learn what it publishes, that the world's most famous publications “sometimes act without ethics”, and that the report in question “struck me as an excess, that is, an intention to hurt Mexico”.

title: AMLO asks who owns the media and calls for ethics
summary: AMLO asked rhetorically who owns the media outlets and what relation the owners have with anchors and businesspeople, citing Televisa and the saying "la nota es la nota", and made a call to media and television owners to put ethics first and not deceive, manipulate or distort reality ("no se engañe, no se manipule, no se tergiverse la realidad").

title: AMLO: the NYT “doesn't investigate, it slanders” on Salgado
summary: Defending Félix Salgado Macedonio amid New York Times reporting on a rape allegation against him, AMLO asked whether the NYT knew Salgado had been elected Guerrero senator two and a half years earlier and that his main accuser was a Guerrero state prosecutor from the PRI government: "o sea, no investigan, calumnian" (they do not investigate, they slander).

title: AMLO: conservatism keeps nearly all journalists “bought or rented”
summary: AMLO said the conservadurismo has almost all journalists "comprados o alquilados, con honrosas excepciones", describing the journalism being practiced as corporativo, proempresarial and protective of corruption; he added the government should speak up without prohibiting or censoring.

title: AMLO criticizes León Krauze: “lack of professionalism… rage”
summary: About an interview fragment by León Krauze, AMLO asked why Krauze does that — "no sólo por falta de profesionalismo, sino por coraje, pierden objetividad, se ofuscan" — and said he understands that a son defends his father, referring to his differences with Enrique Krauze over the defense of the neoliberal model.

title: AMLO dismisses a report on spying on journalists
summary: Asked about a report on alleged spying on journalists, AMLO called it false, cited an El Universal headline ("Espionaje a periodistas es para amedrentarlos") as an example, and said outlets coordinate to question the government without proof. In the same remarks he returned to the idea of a "quién es quién en las mentiras de la semana" section, which he had floated informally the day before (formally launched six days later; see the 2021-06-30 entry).

title: AMLO launches “Quién es quién en las mentiras de la semana”
summary: AMLO formally announced the weekly "Quién es quién en las mentiras de la semana" segment ("vamos a iniciar el quién es quién en las mentiras de la semana, así se va a llamar"), presenting Ana Elizabeth García Vilchis as the official in charge. Its first edition targeted items from El Universal, El País, Forbes, Carlos Loret de Mola, Joaquín López-Dóriga and Raymundo Riva Palacio, among others.
named: Ana Elizabeth García Vilchis; El Universal; El País; Forbes; Carlos Loret de Mola; Joaquín López-Dóriga; Raymundo Riva Palacio

title: AMLO tells Jorge Ramos “I have other data”
summary: Jorge Ramos, self-identifying as being "de Univisión y Reforma," challenged AMLO with homicide and femicide figures (citing over 86,000 killings since the start of the term) and said that "fuera de la burbuja de Palacio Nacional, el país no está en paz." AMLO replied, in what became his best-known rebuttal formula, "ahora sí que yo tengo otros datos," and disputed the characterization of a "burbuja."

title: AMLO denies spying: “no censorship of the media”
summary: Amid the Pegasus spyware coverage, AMLO asserted his government does not spy: "el gobierno no espía nadie, los opositores no son espiados, no hay censura para los medios de información, a nadie se le limitan sus libertades". Contrastive/defensive press-freedom framing (frame D), not an epithet hit.

title: AMLO: “W Radio and El País are the same” via Prisa
summary: Asked about W Radio, AMLO said "W Radio y El País son lo mismo": El País is a Spanish paper owned by the Prisa group, which has great political influence; he stressed the remark was not against the journalists present ("que conste que no es en contra de ustedes").

title: AMLO rejects a press-gag law: the press should regulate itself
summary: In a passage about a proposed press-gag law, AMLO rejected any "ley mordaza" ("nada de eso") and restated the Lerdo maxim in his own words: "que la prensa se controle con la prensa, que se regule con la prensa, que no tenga el Estado que meterse a someter a los medios".

title: AMLO calls Reforma an “immundo pasquín of crude conservatism”
summary: Reading Reforma's front page (Dos Bocas worker death, a Morenista accusing Nahle of union monopoly, border items), AMLO called the paper "convertido en un boletín, un pasquín inmundo del conservadurismo ramplón", saying this is because they were the privileged ones. Distinct dated episode from the existing "pasquín inmundo" entries (2020-09-11, 2020-11-09, 2022-03-01 in incidents_groundtruth.yaml).

title: AMLO quotes Dresser's tweet: “I'm no longer Andrés Manuel but Augusto”
summary: Referring to a Denise Dresser tweet claiming he staged a "golpe de Estado" for granting facilities to companies building major government works, AMLO quoted her words ("ya no soy Andrés Manuel, sino soy Augusto"), said "no se midió", noted she teaches at the ITAM, and added that Reforma's writers are "la mayoría conservadores". The expected phrase is Dresser's tweet, quoted by AMLO to ridicule it (quoted_third_party: true).

title: AMLO accuses Aguayo and Reforma writers of “intellectual dishonesty”
summary: About the CIDE conflict, AMLO said comparing it with the 1968 movement is disproportionate, and that academics like Sergio Aguayo and the Reforma writers who make that comparison commit "mucha deshonestidad intelectual... por el coraje", since they are doctors in social science who know the difference.

title: AMLO responds to the murder of Lourdes Maldonado López
summary: The day after journalist Lourdes Maldonado López was found shot dead in Tijuana, a reporter asked AMLO directly about her 2019 appeal for protection (see the 2019-03-26 entry). AMLO called her killing "lamentable," said an investigation was underway, and noted she had previously been in contact with the government over the labor dispute; he cautioned against assuming a motive before the investigation concluded. Margarito Martínez, a photojournalist, had been killed in Tijuana days earlier.

title: AMLO: Reforma “pontificates” as conservatism's bulletin
summary: Discussing the controversy over the sexual-harassment denunciations against historian Pedro Salmerón and his proposed appointment as ambassador to Panama, AMLO said the media campaign and "linchamiento mediático" must not decide, and that without full information "es el Reforma, el boletín del conservadurismo, el que pontifica y dice quién sí y quién no".

title: Pemex rebuts the “Casa Gris de Houston” report
summary: Pemex director Octavio Romero Oropeza gave a formal rebuttal, at the mañanera, to the "Casa Gris de Houston" reporting — a joint Latinus/ Mexicanos Contra la Corrupción y la Impunidad (MCCI) report (2022-01- 27) and a follow-up Reforma column by Peniley Ramírez (2022-02-05) — which examined a Houston property linked to a Baker Hughes executive rented by the wife of José Ramón López Beltrán, the president's son. Romero presented Pemex contracting data to argue no favoritism was shown to Baker Hughes. This is the direct predecessor to AMLO's own income disclosure about Carlos Loret de Mola two days later (see the 2022-02-11 entry).
named: Latinus; Carlos Loret de Mola; MCCI; Reforma; Peniley Ramírez

title: AMLO discloses Carlos Loret de Mola’s income
summary: Following weeks of "Casa Gris" coverage, AMLO presented figures purporting to show Carlos Loret de Mola's annual income from Televisa, Radiópolis/W Radio, El Universal, Latinus and The Washington Post (totaling "35 millones 200 mil" pesos, by AMLO's account), said "lo considero un mercenario, golpeador, corrupto, en el sentido estricto, ni siquiera periodista," and compared the figure to his own reported salary. Loret de Mola said the government had inflated the numbers, noting he had not worked for Televisa since 2019.
named: Carlos Loret de Mola; Televisa; W Radio; El Universal; Latinus; The Washington Post

title: AMLO again calls Reforma an “immundo pasquín”
summary: Discussing an unrelated Reforma story involving lawyer Diego Fernández de Cevallos's associate and links to Carlos Salinas de Gortari, AMLO called Reforma "boletín del conservadurismo y de un pasquín inmundo que se dedica a atacarnos sin fundamento" and "defensor del salinismo como política" — reusing the same epithet as the 2020-09-11 and 2020-11-09 entries above, now applied a third time.

title: AMLO: the press protects vested interests, not the people
summary: Responding to criticism over insecurity, AMLO said those who “tear their garments” over slain journalists are actually worried that privileges are being fought; he argued this applies not only to Reforma or El Universal but also to the New York Times, the Washington Post, the Financial Times and El País, “because it is a press in general that protects vested-interest groups, not a press that protects the people”.
named: Reforma; El Universal; The New York Times; The Washington Post; Financial Times; El País

title: AMLO denies he would pressure Loret's broadcaster
summary: Asked whether he would pressure the broadcaster that carries Carlos Loret de Mola's program, AMLO answered "cero censura, nada de censura" and said he would not call the owners of the radio station where Loret works to tell them his program bothers them. An explicit denial of pressure in response to a question about pressuring media owners (frame E, documented negative direction).
named: Carlos Loret de Mola; W Radio

title: AMLO: “this journalist staged a setup” — Loret and García Luna
summary: About Carlos Loret de Mola, AMLO said he is famous and very well paid (apartment in the most luxurious building in Mexico City, a 40,000 square meter residence in Valle de Bravo, properties abroad) and that "este periodista hizo un montaje de la detención de unos presuntos delincuentes en contubernio con el jefe de la policía de ese entonces, que era García Luna".

title: AMLO: media complain because they used to be paid by the government
summary: In the context of the discussion of accusations against the press, AMLO said his government neither represses nor censors, but that the media “used to serve the powerful, deceive the people and pretend to be independent”, and that now “they complain because they used to be paid by the government, the potentates paid them”.

title: AMLO: Ricardo Alemán is “a journalist of the conservatives”
summary: About the Baja California violence (Oxxo burnings) and claims that the government orchestrated it, AMLO said "hay quienes sostienen —un periodista de los conservadores, Ricardo Alemán— que todo lo armamos nosotros", that Alemán claims to have palace information to that effect: "o sea, voló, pero alto".

title: AMLO: Anabel Hernández and Ricardo Alemán “overstepped”
summary: Continuing on the Oxxo-burning propaganda, AMLO said "no se midieron, Anabel y Ricardo Alemán", who told journalists in the Patio Central of the National Palace that he had ordered everything to justify the militarization of the country, while Reforma talked of the country burning.

title: AMLO: tribunal sanctioning journalists “never happened even under the gag law”
summary: About the electoral tribunal sanctioning journalists, AMLO asked where the tribunal gets off doing so — "¿cuándo se había visto eso? Ni en la ley mordaza, nunca" — calling it irrational and violatory of freedom of expression and human rights, and predicting it will fail and end up in the trash of history.

title: AMLO: “no one is censored here”
summary: Responding to a reporter, AMLO said "aquí no se censura a nadie, o sea, tú puedes venir y hablar aquí con toda libertad". A press-freedom-concept statement (frame D).

title: AMLO expresses support for Ciro Gómez Leyva after an attack
summary: The morning after gunmen shot at least 12 times at the armored vehicle carrying radio/TV host Ciro Gómez Leyva as he drove home in Mexico City, a few hundred metres from his house in the colonia Florida (the night of 2022-12-15; he was unharmed thanks to the armor), AMLO opened the conference by expressing solidarity ("enviarle mi apoyo a Ciro Gómez Leyva, que ayer fue pues víctima de un atentado"), noted an investigation was underway, and said differences of opinion with him did not change that an attack on any person's life is reprehensible.

title: García Vilchis presents the list of communicators with 1,081-mdp contracts
summary: In the "Quién es quién en las mentiras" segment, Ana Elizabeth García Vilchis presented a list of 36 communicators who received, among them, approximately 1,081 million pesos in government contracts between 2013 and 2018, with Joaquín López-Dóriga first (more than 446 million pesos over three presidential terms, 249 million during Peña Nieto's government alone). Read by García Vilchis (quoted_third_party: true); targets are named journalists (frame A).
named: Joaquín López-Dóriga; Enrique Krauze; Héctor Aguilar Camín; Raymundo Riva Palacio; Ricardo Alemán; Jorge Fernández Menéndez; Adela Micha

title: AMLO: delinquent media-linked firms “don't inform, they manipulate”
summary: Discussing savings from the contract review, AMLO said that of five delinquent companies “about two are media-related”, and that is why “they don't inform, they manipulate; it is not information, it is manipulation”.

title: AMLO calls Carmen Aristegui “a big phony”
summary: Asked about a speech by Carmen Aristegui claiming journalists are attacked, AMLO called her "muy farsante", saying she and many others wanted to keep "el privilegio de agredir y de mentir, y de difamar y de calumniar".

title: AMLO criticizes Televisa's owners over Castañeda and the ethics code
summary: AMLO criticized Televisa's owners for not ensuring that those who use that public concession act according to a code of ethics, asking how they keep Jorge Castañeda as a commentator when he "ofende de manera racista a los pueblos de Oaxaca"; in a follow-up he proposed balance or a code of ethics for programs like Tercer Grado ("todos en contra de nosotros... siempre es paliza").

title: García Vilchis calls science-law coverage a “synchronized swim”
summary: In the weekly "Quién es quién en las mentiras" segment, Ana Elizabeth García Vilchis described coverage across Reforma, El Universal, La Razón, La Silla Rota and several other outlets — all reporting that a Science and Technology Law had been judicially suspended — as "esto es un nado sincronizado de los que acostumbra la oposición," i.e. coordinated ("synchronized swimming"), and said the reporting was false because the relevant injunctions (amparos) benefited only the individuals who filed them.
named: Reforma; El Universal; La Razón; La Silla Rota

title: Nancy Flores asks about MCCI and Latinus funding
summary: Journalist Nancy Flores, of Contralínea, told AMLO about her outlet's reporting on funding for Mexicanos Contra la Corrupción y la Impunidad (MCCI) and Latinus — citing US embassy payments to MCCI and Mexican business-family funding for Latinus — framing it as a "guerra sucia" (dirty war) of media and legal challenges against the government. AMLO replied describing outlets that pay well-known commentators as "medios de información que, yo sostengo, son de manipulación." Contralínea itself has received substantial official government advertising during and after AMLO's term, a fact relevant to reading this exchange.

title: AMLO: Reforma's writers “editorialize, pontificate, lie, slander”
summary: Asked what can be replied to Reforma, AMLO said "nada, ellos editorializan, pontifican, mienten, calumnian, ¿y quién les dice algo? Nadie". The formula recurs in later mañaneras (2023-09-19, 2023-11-15), there addressed to commentators and columnists generally rather than to Reforma; this entry covers the first, dated occurrence only.

title: AMLO: Ciro Gómez Leyva's journalism is “not professional, objective, plural”
summary: On coverage of Morena's internal race, AMLO said Ciro Gómez Leyva was desperate and that “one knows when they're reading from a script”, that what he does “is not professional, objective, plural journalism”, and that his backers “were linked to Calderón”, referring to polls by former Cisen director Guillermo Valdés.

title: AMLO calls the ProPublica/Tim Golden report a slander
summary: The day after ProPublica, Deutsche Welle and InSight Crime independently published three separate reports on the same DEA investigation — Tim Golden's for ProPublica, Anabel Hernández's for Deutsche Welle and Steven Dudley's for InSight Crime that a 2010 DEA investigation had found "substantial evidence" that Sinaloa Cartel-linked money reached AMLO's 2006 campaign, AMLO called the report "completamente falso, es una calumnia," and said of Golden and outlets that ran with the story, "son unos viles calumniadores, aunque los premien como buenos periodistas." The story recurred across many mañaneras through 2024 (see also the 2024-03-08 and 2024-07-19 entries).

title: AMLO: “that is not journalism” — asks what espionage Loret does
summary: About investigations into phone interception, AMLO said those people dedicate themselves to "intervenir teléfonos" and asked what journalism — "eso no es periodismo" — what espionage Loret de Mola does, saying that is what the DEA does: working on phone conversations. Named-journalist delegitimization (frame A; grouped under E in the prior session's informal list).

title: AMLO: “I will sue him” — the García Luna trial lawyer
summary: About a lawyer in the García Luna trial who, outside the procedure, read a card claiming AMLO had received money in the 2006 campaign against Fox (a claim the witness Zambada denied), AMLO said "dije: Lo voy a demandar", but after seeking information — including via ambassador Esteban Moctezuma — he learned such lawyers are legally protected in the United States. Legal-arena episode adjacent to the Tim Golden/Loret coverage (frame E).

title: AMLO reads Natalie Kitroeff’s (NYT) letter, calls it false
summary: AMLO read aloud, in full, a letter and questions sent by New York Times Mexico bureau chief Natalie Kitroeff about a separate reported US investigation into campaign associates and drug-cartel money (distinct from the ProPublica/Tim Golden story), including her contact phone number printed in the letter, and called the paper's questions false, saying "que ustedes son unos falsarios, los del New York Times." YouTube subsequently removed the video of the conference citing its harassment/bullying policy; AMLO showed the same letter again on 2024-02-26 in response.
named: Natalie Kitroeff; The New York Times

title: AMLO calls Tim Golden’s report “mercenary journalism”
summary: Continuing to discuss the ProPublica story, AMLO said Tim Golden had twice been awarded prizes and called the report "un periodismo mercenario," part of a broader argument that the country was living through a "decadencia" rather than a mere crisis.

title: García Vilchis: the WSJ “lies” on arrests; Claudio X. González “lies twice as much”
summary: In the "Quién es quién en las mentiras / en los bots" segment, Ana Elizabeth García Vilchis said "The Wall Street Journal miente sobre detenciones del crimen organizado y Claudio X. González hace segunda y miente el doble", referring to a WSJ article published on February 25. Read by García Vilchis (quoted_third_party: true); outlet target (frame B).

title: AMLO dismisses a new Tim Golden report as a “rehash”
summary: When ProPublica/Tim Golden published a follow-up report (July 2024) citing former DEA officials on the same 2006 campaign-financing allegations, AMLO dismissed it as "un refrito" (a rehash), and had spokesman Jesús Ramírez Cuevas read out a letter exchange between Ramírez and Golden that had preceded the story's publication.

title: AMLO calls Proceso an “immundo pasquín” over the Bartlett story
summary: Discussing a Proceso story reporting that Manuel Bartlett's partner and son had acquired properties near government megaprojects including the Tren Maya route at below-market cost, AMLO defended Bartlett, said the coverage echoed the New York Times/ProPublica pattern, called it "periodismo tendencioso," and said "es lamentable que el Proceso ya se convirtió en un pasquín inmundo al servicio del conservadurismo" — applying the same "pasquín inmundo" epithet used against Reforma (twice) and El Universal in earlier entries, now to Proceso.
